review_notes: I read the whole file and the sibling declarations it relies on. These were levelShuffle_pure in Regroup.lean and the uses of the file's lemmas in FreeCovariance.lean. The file has no simp attributes and no dsimp-unfolding of its own defs apart from the two dsimp only calls. I found no cycle or competing-rule problem. Both findings are about missing simp coverage and are moderate in strength. I could not run Lean, so I did not check whether the proposed @[simp] attribute works as intended. I also did not check for new simp-set interactions in other files. The two shuffle lemmas (_word and _pure) overlap, so I recommend at most one of them as simp.

findings.excerpt:
sourceLevelEmbedding t f hf S i j hS hfree hij n
      (sourceLevelShuffle t f hf S i j hS n x) = levelEmbedding t S hfree hij n x := by
  simp [sourceLevelEmbedding]
findings.problem: This is the canonical cancellation rule for the embedding applied to a shuffled vector. Its right-hand side is strictly simpler. Its proof is already a single `simp [sourceLevelEmbedding]`, so it is a pure simp consequence. It is not tagged @[simp]. Callers that need the rewrite must name it explicitly, as in `rw [←sourceLevelShuffle_bounded,sourceLevelEmbedding_shuffle]` in FreeCovariance.lean. The statement is not in a form that can safely use a default `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp] lemma sourceLevelEmbedding_shuffle ...`. The LHS head is the definition's coercion applied to a shuffle application, and the RHS contains neither. So the rule decreases the term and cannot loop. Explicit `rw [sourceLevelEmbedding_shuffle]` calls (FreeCovariance line 134) can then become `simp only`/`simp`. The `simp [sourceLevelEmbedding]` in its own proof would need care: keep it, or prove it with `simp only [sourceLevelEmbedding, ...]`, since the lemma's own LHS must not be rewritten circularly.
findings.benefit: Downstream goals of the form `sourceLevelEmbedding (sourceLevelShuffle x)` normalise automatically to `levelEmbedding x`. This matches how levelShuffle_pure is already a simp lemma and removes manual rewriting.

findings.excerpt: lemma sourceLevelShuffle_word (n : ℕ) (a : aLetters t S i) (x : BlockParams t S i j n) :
findings.problem: These three pure-tensor evaluation lemmas form a chain. The underlying `levelShuffle_pure` is @[simp], but none of these is. `sourceLevelShuffle_word` is a stepping stone whose RHS still contains `scalarGNSIso ... (a ⊗ₜ pure ...)`. `sourceLevelShuffle_pure` is the fully evaluated form that `scalarGNSIso_pure` is used to reach. Each caller then needs a manual `have result := ...; dsimp only [many abbrevs] at result ⊢; exact result` step. The result is that there is no simp normal form for `sourceLevelShuffle (coe (a ⊗ₜ blockPure x))`. The two shuffle lemmas also overlap in LHS, so tagging both as simp would create competing rules.
findings.proposed_change: Choose `sourceLevelShuffle_pure` as the single simp rule for the `sourceLevelShuffle` (coe (a ⊗ₜ blockPure x)) pattern. Keep `sourceLevelShuffle_word` as a non-simp (or private) helper. Tag `scalarGNSIso_pure` @[simp] so the scalar part evaluates to `PreHilbert.word`. State the lemmas with the abbrevs (`sourceScalar`, `factorFull`, ...) so that the `dsimp only [...]` unfolding in FreeCovariance.sourceLevelShuffle_bounded is unnecessary or reduced.
findings.benefit: Callers such as `sourceLevelShuffle_bounded` could use a short `simp`-based argument instead of an explicit `dsimp only` list of about ten definitions. The simp set would have one canonical evaluation of the shuffle on pure tensors, avoiding the _word/_pure ambiguity.
